content: In Vite, only env vars prefixed VITE_ are exposed to client code via import.meta.env, but that prefix is purely an opt-in exposure gate, not a safety marker -- anything named VITE_* gets embedded verbatim into the built JS bundle and is readable by anyone via devtools/view-source, permanently, even if later removed from a subsequent build (old deployed bundles can still be scraped). Real-world incidents show developers prefixing genuine secrets (API keys, even cloud credentials) with VITE_ as a quick fix to unblock a feature, leading to full compromise when scraped by bots crawling public JS bundles. Correct pattern: never put Stripe secret keys, OAuth client secrets, webhook signing secrets, or DB/session-signing secrets in any VITE_-prefixed variable; those stay server-only env vars (Vercel project env vars) referenced only from serverless functions; only truly public identifiers (Stripe publishable key, Google OAuth client ID) belong in VITE_ vars.
